title: What If Your Crush Could See Your Profile Checks?

lines.text: What if your crush could see your profile checks?

visualStory: Frame one is mid-motion: a large profile card, Mia's pixel portrait, a visible 87 counter and Miko checking it. A tap rolls 87 into 88. No preamble or title banner.
The count stays visible while its eye icon morphs into a notification. Closing the app compresses the profile card into the same delivered receipt instead of resetting the scene.
The receipt folds into Mia's chat. Two progressively typed excuses are backspaced, each with a distinct pixel reaction and synchronized typing sound.
Mia's typing bubble advances into the absurd moving-countries attempt: the same reply card unfolds into a departure ticket. Bring the screenshot in before this detour stalls the story.
The incoming screenshot expands into the same profile-counter layout, now showing Miko's avatar and 93 checks by Mia. Hold the number long enough to read and let Miko react.

Two matching portrait cards and counters settle side by side for the dry punchline. Return the right card into the opening profile layout for a visual loop without pretending to make a seamless spoken sentence.
channelReviewApplication: Problem and counter visible on frame one, with the disclosure established during the hook.
Seconds 4–8 develop the notification consequence through one shared object.
Keep meaningful state changes rather than adding arbitrary cuts or a second explanation.
Pay off the opening number with a larger reciprocal number. Do not insert a long CTA after the joke.
factualBoundaries: The app and feature are fictional. Do not label them as a real Instagram, TikTok or iMessage capability.
Use no real account names, profile photos or private messages.
